title: Your Stock Market's Closing Bell: Why SEBI Says the New Rules Are Here to Stay

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Closing Auction Session (CAS)?
faq.a: The main purpose of CAS is to improve the process of discovering closing prices for F&O-eligible stocks, making them more transparent, robust, and less susceptible to manipulation.

faq.q: Which stocks are affected by CAS?
faq.a: CAS applies to stocks that are part of the Futures & Options (F&O) segment of the Indian stock market.

faq.q: When does the Closing Auction Session take place?
faq.a: The Closing Auction Session runs for 15 minutes, from 3:15 PM to 3:30 PM, for F&O-eligible stocks.

faq.q: Has the market reacted positively to CAS?
faq.a: While SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey acknowledges initial "teething troubles" and feedback from market participants, he believes participation will increase as brokers enable new facilities and investors become more familiar with the system. SEBI's data suggests increased participation and reduced volatility since CAS was introduced.

faq.q: Will SEBI make any changes to CAS in the future?
faq.a: SEBI has stated that while CAS is here to stay, they are analyzing feedback and data to identify any specific constraints or issues that could be improved. Any future adjustments are likely to be incremental rather than structural.
